title: Sentence-boundary-aware KV tiling and prefetch coalescer for continuous batching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce cross-GPU scatter/gather and NVLink traffic for streaming/continuous-batching workloads by aggregating KV cache prefetches around natural text boundaries (sentence/utterance) and coalescing contiguous KV slabs across tensor/pipeline parallel ranks. This ticket implements a lightweight prefetch hinting protocol, a coalescer that merges adjacent KV slices when safe, and an eviction priority that prefers preserving long-prefix hot windows. The feature targets streaming generation workloads (inference with ongoing token appends) and aims to maintain latency SLOs while lowering per-token cost and GPU memory fragmentation.
acceptance_criteria: p95 token generation latency improvement >= 7% on internal streaming benchmark with 8x A100 80GB (long-context workload, 32k tokens) compared to baseline without prefetcher
average NVLink cross-GPU transfer volume reduction >= 12% across the same benchmark
additional GPU memory overhead for coordination metadata <= 5% of total KV cache footprint
no regression in single-GPU throughput for short-context calls (<=2% deviation), validated on runtime-1.21
feature flag gated and backwards compatible with ranks that do not implement the coalescer; rollout plan executed through dedicated canary and A/B tests
technical_design: Overview: Introduce a per-request optional KVHint block that carries (a) prefix-length, (b) sentence-boundary token index heuristics, and (c) prefetch budget. The runtime uses this to decide contiguous KV ranges to coalesce and prefetch before the next batch run.

Coordinator: A low-latency prefetch coordinator runs on tensor-parallel leader rank for each model shard. It aggregates KVHints from inflight streams, computes coalesced slab ranges across pipeline/tensor boundaries, and issues unified prefetch commands to local and remote memory managers.

Coalescer algorithm (high-level): 1) Group inflight streams by neighbouring prefix ranges and boundary alignment; 2) Merge adjacent KV slices if combined size <= prefetch budget and cross-rank alignment conditions satisfied; 3) Emit a single prefetch request per merged range to reduce scatter/gather ops; 4) Track a merge-id to allow safe rollback if generation diverges.

Eviction policy: 'recent-prefix-score' computed as frequency_weight * recent_hits + prefix_length_weight * longest_prefix_retained. Eviction favors removing small, cold micro-slices before larger, long-prefix windows.

Integration with continuous batching: Batch scheduler exposes stream-level boundary events (sentence_end/pause) to the coordinator. When a sentence_end is detected and the next token generation is expected within the latency window, the coordinator triggers prefetch aggregation.
Fallbacks: If any rank lacks the coalescer, runtime falls back to per-stream prefetch; if NVLink is congested, coordinator reduces prefetch budget adaptively.
API change: Optional field 'kv_prefetch_hint' in request object with small schema; documented in API changelog. No breaking changes for existing clients.
Compatibility: Works with tensor and pipeline parallel setups. NUMA and topology hints will be included in a follow-up if initial rollout shows cross-domain hotspots.
Observability: New metrics: kv_coalesce_rate, kv_prefetch_merged_bytes, kv_prefetch_misses, kv_merge_rejections, kv_merge_latency_ms. Add traces for coordinator decision path.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces repeated small NVLink transfers, lowers GPU DRAM fragmentation, improves p95 latency for long-context streaming workloads
Cons: incorrect prefetching can increase memory pressure and cause spill; coalescing logic adds coordination complexity and scheduler contention in extreme high-concurrency scenarios
Mitigations: conservative default budgets, adaptive backoff under spill/pressure signals, and feature flag gating for canary rollout
metrics: KV cache hit ratio and spill rate
Additional GPU memory used for prefetch metadata
rollout_plan: 1) Internal simulation and synthetic benchmarks (locally and on ci-perf) using long-context streaming traces - complete by 2025-02-28
2) Small dedicated canary (2 customer-dedicated pools) behind feature flag for 72 hours monitoring kv metrics - target start 2025-03-07
3) Expand canary to 10% hosted traffic for selected low-risk models with A/B measurement (2 weeks)
4) Full rollout in runtime-1.21 if metrics stable and no regression observed in short-context workloads
comments: 2025-02-18 Asha Patel: Created ticket. Initial idea from streaming ops notes — capturing sentence boundaries to prefetch contiguous KV ranges to reduce cross-rank scatter/gather.

2025-02-22 Sofia Ramirez (Design): Reviewed UX for feature flag and API. Suggested keeping kv_prefetch_hint optional and tiny to avoid client churn. Recommend documenting common heuristics for sentence-boundary markers.

2025-02-25 Dmitry Kozlov (Infra): Concern: risk of increased NVLink congestion if too many coalesced prefetches fire concurrently. Proposed adding a pacing limiter tied to current NVLink throughput metric.

2025-02-28 Marco Huang: Prototype results: synthetic long-context trace showed 11% p95 improvement and 14% NVLink reduction in lab with budget=128KB. Peak additional memory 3.2% (within target). Need extended tests across model families.
